name: Centaurus
introduction: is the Centaur, often identified with the wise Chiron, teacher of heroes. One of the largest constellations in the sky, it wraps around the Southern Cross and contains the nearest stars to the Sun. It is best seen from the Southern Hemisphere in autumn evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Centaurus is our nearest neighbor. [Rigel Kentaurus](hip:71683), Alpha Centauri, is a pair of Sun-like stars that orbit each other every 80 years, about 4.4 light-years away. A third star, the red dwarf [Proxima Centauri](id:proxima-centauri), is slightly closer, making it the nearest known star to the Sun. In 2016, astronomers discovered a planet orbiting Proxima in its habitable zone.
Alpha Centauri and [Agena](hip:68702), also called Hadar, are the Pointers. Together they guide observers to the Southern Cross and the south celestial pole.

image.caption: Star View schematic · catalogue positions, north up and east left
image.alt: The Pointers, Alpha Centauri and Hadar, together with the long bar of the Southern Cross, lead to the south celestial pole.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: To the naked eye, [Rigel Kentaurus](hip:71683) is the third-brightest star in the night sky; a small telescope splits it into two. [Agena](hip:68702) appears almost as bright but lies about 390 light-years away: a system of three hot, blue stars, thousands of times as luminous as the Sun.

[Menkent](hip:68933) is an orange giant about 60 light-years away. [Epsilon Centauri](hip:66657) and [Eta Centauri](hip:71352) are among the blue stars of the Scorpius–Centaurus association, a large family of young stars that spans this part of the sky.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Omega Centauri is the largest globular cluster in the Milky Way, a ball of about ten million stars that may be the core of a dwarf galaxy swallowed long ago. In 2024, astronomers found evidence for a medium-sized black hole at its center. Nearby, Centaurus A, about 12 million light-years away, is a giant galaxy crossed by a dark dust lane with jets powered by a supermassive black hole. The Boomerang Nebula is the coldest known natural place in the universe, about one degree above absolute zero.
